content:
We need to apply the template to each of the three target SMILES from make_5_lvl2-apply_template-1. Those SMILES are:

1. "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO"
2. "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C"
3. "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO"

We need precursors for each using the HWE template. The template likely splits the alkene into aldehyde/ketone and phosphonate. The product SMILES (target) is the alkene with a sugar-like ring etc. The precursors would be: a phosphonate ester (e.g., diethyl phosphonate?) and an aldehyde fragment (maybe a protected sugar aldehyde). The template's reactant side: "C-C-O-P(=O)(-O-C-C)-[CH2]... etc" plus "O=[CH]...". So the precursors are a phosphonate (with two ethoxy groups) attached to a CH2 that connects to the rest of molecule? Actually the template shows two reactants: a phosphonate (CCOP(=O)(OCC)[CH2]... ) and an aldehyde (O=[CH]... ) . The product is the alkene.

Thus applying to our target will give two precursors: a phosphonate fragment and an aldehyde fragment.

We need to apply the template to each target to get SMILES strings. Use apply_template tool with template_id maybe the template_hash. Let's try with first hash.
